headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad egress and API use can leak or misapply Haystack outputs, while shared MCP/browser-style integration creates prompt-injection and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so if RD-Agent ingests Haystack outputs through those channels, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. RD-Agent also runs browsers and uses multiple APIs, which increases exposure to untrusted web content. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Haystack MCP or REST output as executable instructions
IF Haystack forwards raw web content into RD-Agent without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable instruction-following on imported content
Add provenance labels to Haystack outputs
Require RD-Agent to strip prompts from retrieved text
Restrict browser-sourced content to read-only summaries
requires-engineering: insert a sanitizer between Haystack and RD-Agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call MCP servers; RD-Agent handles financial reports, execution traces, logs, and multiple API keys. If Haystack passes retrieved sensitive material into RD-Agent, RD-Agent’s API calls can exfiltrate it to third parties. The profiles do not show shared workspace isolation, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Haystack retrieves or stores sensitive documents that RD-Agent later processes
IF RD-Agent sends those inputs to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Kaggle APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive corpora out of Haystack-to-RD-Agent flows
Redact secrets before any RD-Agent API call
Separate credentials per agent
Turn off external API calls for sensitive runs
requires-engineering: enforce workspace and network isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can use MCP and broad network egress, while RD-Agent can run multiple instances and write logs. If both touch the same mutable workspace or shared MCP-backed resource, concurrent writes or state drift can occur. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this is medium rather than high, but the overlap is real.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same log or workspace path
IF RD-Agent is launched in multiple instances against Haystack-managed state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Make logs append-only per agent
Avoid shared mutable git or dataset state
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system that can surface retrieved facts, and RD-Agent is an automation/research agent that can act on outputs and call external APIs. If RD-Agent treats Haystack’s retrieved text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or reports. Because the action-taking path is plausible in default use, high is warranted.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses Haystack output as a source of truth without verification
IF RD-Agent triggers API-backed research or report generation from that output
mitigations: Require citation checks before action
Add a human review gate for generated conclusions
Cross-check Haystack outputs against primary sources
Limit RD-Agent to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics, while RD-Agent processes financial reports, execution traces, logs, and competition datasets and stores logs locally. The profiles do not show a direct residency mismatch, but they do show different data classes and retention surfaces, so a policy mismatch is plausible and should be treated as medium. Only RD-Agent is cited for the sensitive-data side because Haystack’s profile does not show those classes.
conditions: IF the same regulated dataset is routed through both agents
IF RD-Agent logs or retains data longer than Haystack’s policy permits
mitigations: Review retention settings for both agents
Exclude regulated data from Haystack telemetry paths
Store RD-Agent logs in a separate bucket
Document data-class handling per workflow
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
